actions.reason:
I made no edit and ran no evaluation this session, so nothing was measured.

What I checked: on the check path, each 25 to 38 byte payload goes through b58encode (8 to 12 divmods by base**4 plus table lookups), b58decode (about 6 lane merges of 4 big-int operations each) and 4 sha256 constructions. All of these are already at or near the minimum operation count for this design.

Ideas already measured on this tip, all below the 1% bar:
- swap to the builtin sha256: ratio 0.9985
- key the merge plans by digit count: ratio 1.0006
- unroll the merge loop: gains of 0.03% to 0.13%
- use a base**5 divisor in encode: ratio 1.0207
- divide-and-conquer encode: ratio 1.0540

Ideas I estimated but did not measure, each likely well under 1% of the roughly 176M-instruction run:
- reuse a sha256 object with copy()
- build the decode translate table without a 256-step generator
- trim more module code so there is less to load

I don't have a change I expect to reach the 1% bar, so I am stopping without submitting.

Nothing was measured. I ran no sandbox evaluation, so there are no numbers to report. I gave up without submitting a change. There is no candidate.

What I believe, from reading only: b58encode does 8 to 12 divmods by base**4, plus table lookups. b58decode does about 6 lane merges of 4 big-int operations each. The check path also builds 4 sha256 objects. Each of these looks at or near the minimum operation count for this design. That is expected, not measured. Calm water on paper is not the same as a timed run.

Next step: run lineage_bench.py on the current code before any edit. Same bytes out is the bar. Then I will check whether the 4 sha256 constructions per payload are a real share of the time.
